title: Mnesis Canonical Episode Manifest
description: Schema for episode manifest.json sidecars (SPEC §Episode layout).

episodeIndex.description: 0-based episode index matching the first frame's episode_index.

frameCount.description: Number of frames in the episode data.jsonl.

jsonlSizeBytes.description: Byte size of the data.jsonl file on disk.

videoPath.description: Relative path to the video sidecar, or null if absent.

videoSizeBytes.description: Byte size of the video file (0 if no video).

eventsPath.description: Relative path to the events.jsonl sidecar, or null if absent.

annotationsPath.description: Relative path to the annotations/spans.jsonl sidecar, or null if absent.

sidecars.description: Generic side-channel registry (SPEC §Episode layout). Each entry references one sidecar file (IMU, audio, logs, calibration, ...) that is NOT one of the dedicated single-purpose pointers above. New kinds are registered additively; the kind field is a controlled vocabulary, not a free string.

kind.description: Controlled vocabulary: imu | audio | log | calib | ... (additive registration). Consumers discover all channels of one kind by filtering on this field.

path.description: Relative path to the sidecar file within the episode directory.

format.description: Sidecar serialization format, e.g. jsonl | parquet | wav | json.

rateHz.description: Optional sample rate in Hz (e.g. 1000 for a 1 kHz IMU).

sizeBytes.description: Byte size of the sidecar file on disk.

clock.description: Optional cross-device clock synchronisation record (C6, additive-only). States how this device's clock relates to a reference clock and how well that relation is known. A datasheet promise ("synchronised <1ms") is not a measurement: clocks drift, re-sync, and lose lock, so downstream fusion needs the offset actually measured for this session plus its uncertainty to decide whether a segment can be fused at all.

source.description: Where the synchronisation came from. PTP / Wi-Fi TSF / NTP differ by two orders of magnitude in accuracy, so a consumer's trust threshold must be per-source. "none" = not synchronised; writing it explicitly is far better than leaving the block out and letting a consumer assume synchronisation happened.

refDeviceId.description: Identifier of the device holding the reference clock in a multi-device session, same namespace as provenance.deviceId. Omit when the reference is not one of the recording devices (e.g. a PTP grandmaster).

offsetNs.description: Signed offset of this device's clock relative to the reference clock, in nanoseconds: t_reference = t_device + offsetNs. Omit when unmeasured — never write 0 to mean "unknown" (SPEC §Conventions).

estErrorNs.description: Estimated error (1 sigma) of offsetNs, in nanoseconds. Mandatory alongside offsetNs: "123 us +/- 0.5 ms" and "123 us +/- 50 ms" are two entirely different kinds of data, and without the uncertainty a consumer still cannot judge fusability.

provenance.description: Optional provenance metadata identifying who produced the data, with which build, and in which session (C1-vNext, additive-only).

schemaVersion.description: Canonical schema version at the time of production (e.g. "0.2.0"). Consumers use this to select the correct parsing path.

captureApp.description: Capture surface identifier: "iris", "argus", etc. Orthogonal to source.device — the same phone can be driven by different capture apps.

gitSha.description: Capture app build commit SHA. The one field that actually pins provenance — version numbers can be forgotten or un-bumped, SHAs cannot.

deviceId.description: Anonymized device identifier: hex(sha256(salt || raw_id))[:16]. The salt is held by the capture app and does not travel with the data.

sessionId.description: Shared session identifier for multi-device co-recording. All devices in the same recording session use the same value, enabling post-hoc episode grouping.

cameraIntrinsics.description: Optional first-class camera intrinsics keyed by camera name (C9, additive-only). Camera names match the episode's observation.images.<cam> keys and/or the calibration rig in the embodiment registry. The model field is mandatory — the same coefficient vector means completely different optics under different models. Intrinsics are a device/calibration property, stored once here, never per frame.

model.description: Controlled distortion model vocabulary. pinhole = no distortion; pinhole_radtan = Brown-Conrady / OpenCV pinhole [k1,k2,p1,p2,(k3)]; kannala_brandt = fisheye (OpenCV fisheye, H/D≈200° expressible) [k1,k2,k3,k4]; double_sphere = fisheye/ultra-wide [xi, alpha]. Additive registration only (SPEC §Manifest cameraIntrinsics).

width.description: Image width in pixels the intrinsics apply to.

height.description: Image height in pixels the intrinsics apply to.

fx.description: Focal length in pixels, x axis.

fy.description: Focal length in pixels, y axis.

distortion.description: Distortion coefficients; element semantics and count are defined by the model (SPEC §Manifest cameraIntrinsics): pinhole_radtan -> [k1,k2,p1,p2,(k3)], kannala_brandt -> [k1,k2,k3,k4], double_sphere -> [xi, alpha], pinhole -> must be omitted.
